description: The argument to the :default preset becomes :reviewer(arg0). It carries the `team:` prefix and the bare slug, without the organisation: Renovate splits reviewers on that prefix and posts the remainder as a team reviewer, so `OneLiteFeatherNET/falco-maintainers` would be sent as a user name and rejected. The team holds admin on this repository and is the same owner .github/CODEOWNERS names.

The :minestom flavor only fixes version ordering for a pinned `net.minestom:minestom`. Falco resolves Minestom through mycelium-bom and pins no version of its own today, so the flavor is inert here and kept for the moment a version does get pinned.

The last packageRule of the :default preset, "Security fixes bypass the schedule, the cooldown period and any grouping", puts `isVulnerabilityAlert: true` where a matcher belongs. That key is an option, not a matcher, so the rule applies to every maven, github-tags and gradle-version update: each one is handled as a vulnerability fix (`vulnerabilityFixStrategy=lowest` proposes only the next version, hence step-by-step PRs), loses its group and its cooldown period, ignores `schedule:officeHours` and gets the `security` label. The packageRules below, which Renovate applies after the preset's, take that back: the first one resets the options the preset rule overwrote, the following ones repeat the preset rules that set a group, a cooldown period or a schedule, in their original order. Real vulnerability alerts keep their exemptions through the top-level `vulnerabilityAlerts` block. All of this can go once the preset gives that rule a real matcher. The `security` label cannot be taken back from here, because `addLabels` only ever accumulates.

Falco's own version in README.md and docs/ is raised twice over: Release Please rewrites the snippets carrying an `x-release-please` marker in the release pull request (extra-files in release-please-config.json), and the regex customManager below picks up the ones without a marker, so a missed marker costs one Renovate pull request and not a stale install snippet.

packageRules.description: Undo the preset rule that treats every update as a vulnerability fix: same match as that rule, restores the office-hours schedule and the default cooldown period
Restore preset rule: internal artifacts, group and cooldown period
Restore preset rule: own reusable workflows, group and cooldown period
Restore preset rule: remaining GitHub Actions, group
Restore preset rule: major updates, longer cooldown period
Restore preset rule: Gradle wrapper minor and major, longer cooldown period
Restore preset rule: patches, group, schedule and cooldown period

customManagers.description: Keep the coordinates in the install snippets of the README and of docs/ on the released version. One rule for all five published artifacts: the artifact name is captured rather than templated, so a module is covered the moment a snippet mentions it. `falco-benchmarks` and `falco-demo` are deliberately not listed because they are never published. A consumer declares the BOM inside a `platform("…")` call rather than a bare `implementation("…")` one, so the first match string covers both call forms; the second one covers a Maven `<dependency>` or `<dependencyManagement>` entry, and `depNameTemplate` joins the two captured halves into the one dependency name both forms share. Release Please raises the marked snippets in the release pull request (see release-please-config.json); this rule catches the ones without a marker, such as a snippet that also names Minestom, whose version a marker would rewrite as well.
